factsheet_lines_1_indexed.3: 1. Oliver Stone - A worker at MacMillan's Lumber Mill who discovered the Ashen Note.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.4: 2. Edith Granger - A local historian in Birchtown dedicated to uncovering the town's past.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.5: 3. Professor Harold Bell - A linguist from a nearby university who aided in the attempt to decipher the Ashen Note.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.6: 4. MacMillan's Lumber Mill - The central site of the Ashen Note discovery and community gatherings.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.7: 5. Birchtown Community - The collective group of townspeople engaged with the mystery of the Ashen Note.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.8: 6. Birchtown Folklore Society - A group formed post-incident to preserve and explore local stories and legends.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.12: 1. Discovery of the Ashen Note (1946) - Oliver Stone finds the charred note while demolishing an old furnace at MacMillan's Lumber Mill.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.13: 2. Initial Analysis (1946) - Edith Granger and Professor Harold Bell begin their investigation into the note's meaning, drawing on local folklore and linguistic expertise.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.14: 3. Community Speculation (1946-1947) - Townspeople gather at the mill, developing theories on the note's significance, ranging from hidden treasures to espionage.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.15: 4. Formation of the Birchtown Folklore Society (1947) - In response to the community's interest, a society is formed to explore and document local legends.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.16: 5. Closure of the Investigation (1948) - Despite efforts, the note's origins and message remain unresolved, becoming part of local lore.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.20: 1. Birchtown - A small, industrious town focused on lumber production and post-war rebuilding.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.21: 2. MacMillan's Lumber Mill - The main site for both lumber processing and the discovery of the Ashen Note.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.22: 3. Birchtown Historical Society - A local institution involved in the preservation of the town's history and artifacts.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.23: 4. Nearby University - The institution where Professor Harold Bell works, providing academic resources for the investigation.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.27: 1. 1946 - The year the Ashen Note was discovered, marking the beginning of the incident.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.28: 2. 1946-1947 - A period of intense community engagement and speculative discussion about the note.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.29: 3. 1947 - The year the Birchtown Folklore Society was established.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.30: 4. 1948 - The year when active investigation into the note ceased, with no definitive conclusion reached.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.34: 1. Post-War Rebuilding - The demand for lumber and economic revitalization create a bustling environment in Birchtown, leading to the discovery of the note during routine mill operations.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.35: 2. Intrigue and Mystery - The cryptic nature of the Ashen Note, combined with its mysterious script and symbols, captivates the community's imagination and fuels widespread speculation.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.36: 3. Historical and Cultural Curiosity - The note's potential ties to local folklore and wartime activities inspire efforts to decode its meaning, reflecting the town's interest in its own history and legends.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.37: 4. Community Cohesion - The incident brings the townspeople together, fostering a shared sense of mystery and cultural identity despite the lack of resolution.

items.instruction: Under the confirmation rules a preserved unit (assertion_only or conflict_flagged) must be its own group, and that group's statement must be the unit's source_statement copied verbatim, with no added or removed punctuation. Fix it in one of two ways. (a) Only for assertion_only: if an exact factsheet line supports the assertion as stated, set status "grounded", give the exact line(s) as evidence, and say why in "note". The unit may then stay in its group. (b) Otherwise give the unit its own group: a new id ground-<event>-<nn> with an unused nn, source_unit_ids [the unit], statement = source_statement verbatim, and a grouping_rationale. Remaining members keep their group. Every distinct answer label of every group must have exactly one source_qa record with two closed-book questions (AUTHORING-SPEC.md). Move, keep or write source_qa records so this holds, with unit_id set to the record's group id. For this item, option (b) means setting this group's statement to the source_statement verbatim. Then check that its source_qa questions still follow the rules.
